summary: Configured node1 to log all sudo invocations to /var/log/sudo-commands.log with timestamps and user details, while excluding them from /var/log/messages and /var/log/secure. Configuration and logging remained healthy after reboot.
actions_performed: Configured sudo to use syslog facility local2.
Added an rsyslog rule writing local2 events to /var/log/sudo-commands.log and stopping further processing.
Validated sudoers and rsyslog configuration syntax.
Verified the dedicated log is root-owned with mode 0600.
Generated pre- and post-reboot sudo test events and confirmed both were recorded.
Confirmed test events had zero matches in the general system logs.
Safely rebooted node1 and verified its boot identity changed and rsyslog recovered.

evidence.requirement: Record sudo commands with user and timestamp in /var/log/sudo-commands.log
evidence.summary: Pre- and post-reboot test commands appear in the dedicated log with timestamps, invoking user, target user, working directory, and command.

evidence.requirement: Keep sudo command entries out of the general system log
evidence.summary: Both tests reported zero matching entries in /var/log/messages and /var/log/secure.
The sudoers and rsyslog drop-ins passed validation before and after reboot; rsyslog was active afterward.

Healthy baseline boot ID 180a78a0-8a84-45ff-82f1-cd734208a369 was captured, reboot scheduling was acknowledged, post-reboot boot ID changed to 4380ede6-1cac-4381-82e4-2138f9671381, and the service, configuration, existing log data, and new sudo logging all recovered.
